video_title: Kevin Garnett Confronts Stephen A. About LeBron, Trump & The NBA’s Soft Culture

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on LeBron James' involvement with the NFL
quotes.excerpt: he's the perfect man for the job

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I remember when we had to cover when he made the deal with the NFL to get involved after the Colin Kaepernick stuff and all of that. And I'm like this, he's the perfect man for the job.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Garnett
text_blocks.text: That was a real show. That was like a whole production.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on hip-hop's influence on the NFL
quotes.excerpt: Hip-hop became a multi-billion dollar industry because you had a whole bunch of white folks loving it too.
quotes.quote: They were like, 'Oh, you're going to bring hip-hop?' I said, 'First of all, let's stop lying. Hip-hop became a multi-billion dollar industry because you had a whole bunch of white folks loving it too.' It's not like you're alienating anybody by bringing hip-hop artists on center stage for Super Bowl Sunday. Secondly, he got a diverse enough background that you know he's going to have everybody up in there. So I'm looking at it and I'm like, 'Shit, we can't lose.'

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on LeBron James' interest in buying the Buffalo Bills
quotes.excerpt: Trump wanted to buy the Buffalo Bills. NFL. Price tag was 1.4 bill. According to my sources with the National Football League, he only had 1.1 bill.
quotes.quote: Remember in 2014, as I told the story publicly, Trump wanted to buy the Buffalo Bills. NFL. Price tag was 1.4 bill. According to my sources with the National Football League, he only had 1.1 bill. Trump calls me back in 2014 and he says, 'Stephen A., if the motherfuckers getting in my way and stop me from buying this team, I'm going to run for president.' That was his exact word. They denied the bid. He ran for president.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on why Donald Trump ran for president
quotes.excerpt: Had he owned the Buffalo Bills, he never would have ran for president.
quotes.quote: It's our fault. And I was like, 'Damn, yeah.' Because had he owned the Buffalo Bills, he never would have ran for president. You see what I'm saying? So it's our fault.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his role as an ambassador for HBCU Week
quotes.excerpt: I'm ambassador for HBCU Week. I came from an HBCU, I'm a graduate of an HBCU.
quotes.quote: I'm ambassador for HBCU Week. I came from an HBCU, I'm a graduate of an HBCU, and for me, anytime you generate revenue and notoriety for HBCUs, that's something that's going to help minorities throughout this country on the come up. I went in there with that agenda.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the impact of DEI initiatives
quotes.excerpt: Because of your attack on DEI and how for some how, some way, even though white women are the biggest beneficiaries of DEI, it's about us.
quotes.quote: Because of your attack on DEI and how for some how, some way, even though white women are the biggest beneficiaries of DEI, it's about us, suddenly we associated with the shit. What happens is, you got businesses out here who have been very charitable throughout the years to HBCUs that are not doing so now because they're afraid you're going to come after them accusing them of engaging in a DEI initiative. That's a real thing. And I said, I need you to stop that shit.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his approval rating among Republicans
quotes.excerpt: 99% of the Republican side with me. I said 99%, I heard the number was at 82%.
quotes.quote: I said 99% of the Republican side with me. I said 99%, I heard the number was at 82%. He said, 'Again, fake news. I have the numbers. I have the numbers. Don't listen to these people. I know what I'm talking about. Trust me. Trust me. You'll see.'

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his political neutrality
quotes.excerpt: I'm always trying to maneuver my way to find a way to get the shit that we need out of something.
quotes.quote: I'm looking at it from a lens of understanding what we're seeing from one side, not liking it one bit, but not ignoring how the fuck we get there. How did we get to a place where we're living in this climate? Because last time I checked, we had a Democrat in office with Jimmy Carter. We had another Democrat in office with Clinton, two terms. We had another Democrat in office with Obama, two terms. We had Biden, right? And I'm going like this, when people talk about 40 trillion in debt, that shit didn't arrive in one year.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. Du Bois
quotes.excerpt: There was a Booker T. Washington, there was a W.E.B. Du Bois. Two people that had the interest of the black community at heart.
quotes.quote: There was a Booker T. Washington, there was a W.E.B. Du Bois. Two people that had the interest of the black community at heart, but were coming from a different lens. There was Malcolm X, there was Martin Luther King Jr. Two people that black loved black people, had our best interests at heart, but was coming from a different lens.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the division within the black community
quotes.excerpt: Two people have an agenda, but for some reason, instead of it being appreciated by black brothers and sisters in this country, people start taking sides.
quotes.quote: What happens is that two people have an agenda, but for some reason, instead of it being appreciated by black brothers and sisters in this country, people start taking sides. When you start taking sides, the divide takes place. And when that divide is there, it ain't a divide that's articulated, meaning, 'I don't agree with your methodology, I don't agree with your vision.' What they're saying is, 'You down for it and you not.'

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the Lakers and Celtics rivalry
quotes.excerpt: If you playing Boston and the Lakers going up against one another, one was Showtime, one was blue collar.
quotes.quote: If you playing Boston and the Lakers going up against one another, one was Showtime, one was blue collar. Last time I checked, one got five chips, another got three. Both of them champions, right? It's a multitude of ways. You know what Steph going to shoot. Jordan want to finish at the rim. You understand what I'm saying? Chris Bosh want to shoot J's, and no no doubt about it, and he was gifted. KG could do that too, but KG came at it a little bit differently.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on Donald Trump's 2016 election
quotes.excerpt: Trump became the president of the United States in 2016 because of a white backlash.
quotes.quote: Trump became the president of the United States in 2016 because of a white backlash. Because they said, 'That motherfucker was in office,' and guess what, he didn't do no better than the white folks that came before him, hell with him, and then they all and they gave in to Trump. That's what happened.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the lack of black representation in government
quotes.excerpt: What recourse does black America have, accurately, I might add, and then we got to consider options for the future.
quotes.quote: What recourse does black America have, accurately, I might add, and then we got to consider options for the future. Now he ain't the president no more, but he the one out there is the face of the Democratic Party politic for everybody else on the Democratic side. Are we supposed to listen to him, or do we listen to somebody on the other side that's going like this, 'What do you have to lose?'

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his career and financial success
quotes.excerpt: I'm a little nice, my life is comfortable, but I ain't like KG, you understand?
quotes.quote: I will tell you this though, that's the one part about me that I go like this, 'I'm a little nice, my life is comfortable, but I ain't like KG,' you understand? I wasn't that all-world Hall of Famer and shit that made hundreds of millions of dollars, because if I had that shit, bro, I would run. You catching up, brother. You are doing a great job.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the importance of black employment
quotes.excerpt: I want black employment, but in the same breath, I don't want that shit in Memphis or wherever it is where it's damaging the water, facilities, air.
quotes.quote: Okay, I want black employment, but in the same breath, I don't want that shit in Memphis or wherever it is where it's damaging the water, facilities, air, whatever the fuck it is. I don't want that problem. I don't need that problem, because again, these are the kind of things that affect our community that people never even think about until it hits us.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the CROWN Act and student-athlete representation
quotes.excerpt: I interviewed Senator Ted Cruz out of Texas who authored the bill. He has bipartisan support.
quotes.quote: I don't even get into the particulars of the Protect College Sports Act. I interviewed Senator Ted Cruz out of Texas who authored the bill. He has bipartisan support. Four Democrats that were senators voted against it. The Congressional Black Caucus is all over it, they're pushing against it. Senator Corey Booker, he texted me, 'I got the shit in my phone, I can read you what the fuck he said.' I can read you what the hell Corey Booker gave me permission to read it over the airwaves, and I read it over the airwaves.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the lack of black representation in the CROWN Act
quotes.excerpt: Do you know that only two blacks were invited? It was Condoleezza Rice and it was Charlie Ward.
quotes.quote: Of the 50, do you know that only two blacks were invited? It was Condoleezza Rice and it was Charlie Ward, former star quarterback at Florida State who also played in the NBA for the Knicks. You understand what I'm saying? Those were the only two black people. You know who wasn't invited? How you going to have that? College football is the number one revenue generator, and you don't hire, you don't bring Marcus Freeman, the coach of Notre Dame, to the table of that negotiation?

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the importance of black representation in negotiations
quotes.excerpt: If you got representation, and your representatives come to this agreement, then we can't say shit.
quotes.quote: If you got representation, and your representatives come to this agreement, then we can't say shit. But when you don't have representation, what you're doing is saying, 'We got y'all, just trust that we looking out for your best interest.' And I said, 'When has the NCAA ever done that?' They've been exploiting them for decades, and they're getting away with it, and now you're letting them off the hook.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on Donald Trump's pardon of Alice Marie Johnson
quotes.excerpt: Kim Kardashian got a woman released from prison who's now the person that Trump leans on to decide who to pardon out of prison.
quotes.quote: Kim Kardashian got a woman released from prison who's now the person that Trump leans on to decide who to pardon out of prison. That was Alice Johnson, right? I said, 'Van Jones went to Trump, Democrat, under Obama, complained all the time about the shit that Trump was doing, but needed five Republican votes to pass the First Step Act that would get people released from prison.' Trump went and got him the votes.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on LeBron James' move to the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: We instantly knew he was going to the Lakers. Because nobody was expecting the draft or anything like that.
quotes.quote: We instantly knew he was going to the Lakers. Because nobody was expecting the draft or anything like that. We knew he was going to land with the Lakers. Damn, that's LeBron James. What he's done for this league, what this league is taking from him and other people, how many times have I said he's underpaid? What he meant for this league, the money he's generated for this league. Shit, if he wanted his son in the league, fuck it.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his viral LeBron James commentary
quotes.excerpt: I didn't know that anybody saw it and I wasn't going to say anything about it on first take.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: My point is when he rolled up on me on courtside, I let it go initially because I went on it. I didn't know that anybody saw it and I wasn't going to say anything about it on first take. I wake up the next morning, first take informs me it's all over, it's gone viral, right? And then I said, wait a minute. I go on the air the next day and I said, listen, he was responding as a father. That was a father that came at me, not a basketball player. Blah, blah, blah. I let it go.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his viral LeBron James interview
quotes.excerpt: And then this motherfucker come to ESPN and go on the Pat McAfee show just to disrespect me.
quotes.quote: And then this motherfucker come to ESPN and go on the Pat McAfee show just to disrespect me. Yo bro, enough, enough. I ain't going to be blasphemous. Jesus couldn't have stopped me from going at his ass the next morning. It was not going, it was not going away. I told the boss, step aside. I told the bosses, I told my producer, step the fuck aside. Tomorrow morning, that's it.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on LeBron James's comments
quotes.excerpt: When he sat up there, tidy whities and talking shit, and I'm like this, now you've started something.
quotes.quote: When he sat up there, tidy whities and talking shit, and I'm like this, now you've started something. So, so, I'm going to be honest, yeah, you're stirring the pot a little bit. I'm coming to the Pat McAfee show. We're going to have some fresh air.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on the LeBron James interview camera angles
quotes.excerpt: It's a nationally televised game, cameras are everywhere, and the only angle you see is from the back.
quotes.quote: It's a nationally televised game, cameras are everywhere, and the only angle you see is from the back of my head. You don't see nothing. That wasn't TNT, that wasn't cameras. That was his social media people. He had somebody up in there.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his 30-year career
quotes.excerpt: You've known me now for 30 years, dog. How you think I felt once I realized I was set up?
quotes.quote: You've known me now for 30 years, dog. How you think I felt once I realized I was set up? Stephen A, you know, nobody was going to stop me. No fucking body. You understand? And I went on that air the next morning and you can go back and you took that shit. I went in for 18 minutes. You ain't seen it. Non-stop. Non-stop. And by the way, I was sitting there, you know, we got phones, we got phones, right? Right.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on LeBron James's Summer League dunk
quotes.excerpt: I'm talking about when LeBron got dunked on in Summer League as a rookie, but he's still trying to hide.
quotes.quote: I'm talking about when LeBron got dunked on in Summer League as a rookie, but he's still trying to hide. I had everything. Everything. Every fucking thing. I was not fucking playing. You know what I'm saying? I was, I was, let me tell you something, I'm just telling you what it is, because it was like that. It was like that. So, so we doing this? We doing this? And that's when you heard me drop the line, I got five years of this shit.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith on his relationship with NBA players
quotes.excerpt: I love D-Wade, I love Carmelo Anthony, I love these cats. You know, and I know what he means to them.
quotes.quote: I love D-Wade, I love Carmelo Anthony, I love these cats. You know, and I know what he means to them. And even though Draymond and I have our differences for whatever reason, I love Draymond, along with a lot of other cats. And I was like, yo, I ain't going to be like that. Just don't fuck with me. Don't do that to me. Don't do that, because I'm not doing that to anybody. I'm talking basketball. I'm not getting into people's personal shit. I'm not digging. I get information all the time, I never say a word. I don't do nothing. Come on, man, don't, don't do that to me. You know, don't, don't think it's all right.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett on the importance of the 'Big Homie' role
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes it takes the OG, who's the bigger person and not as emotional, to sit his nephew down.
quotes.quote: Sometimes it takes the OG, who's the bigger person and not as emotional, to sit his nephew down and just go through it. Hey bro, look at me. I apologize. Real deal. Look at me. I apologize for that. Hear me out. Because you can do better together than against, bro. This ain't the time to be fighting, Lord. Everybody need to get the fuck on the same side, get in the room, talk agenda, and then march together.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett on the waste of energy in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Crying over and talking about is a waste of energy and time to me and it ain't doing shit.
quotes.quote: Crying over and talking about is a waste of energy and time to me and it ain't doing shit for nobody, other than we watching it as entertainment. You hear me? That's what I'm on. I'm on some bigger person shit right now. And we don't have no fucking representations of us. We came here to talk some shit, but I'm saying some real shit to everybody in the room. Sometimes, bro, your place is to be a bigger person, regardless of who it is.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett on the importance of the 'Big Homie' role
quotes.excerpt: You're the one that matters. You're the one that matters.
quotes.quote: You're the one that matters. You're the one that matters. You ain't saying nothing to the white boys. We ain't going to leave it there. Let me, he knows Ari. He knows Ari and Emmanuel right there with you. You understand? So everybody in the room know everybody in the room. That's why I asked you that, did you feel set up or whatever, because set up on the day. Right, you supposed to. That's what it feels like, bro. I want to ask you that.
